answer: Because the entropy is measured at the ember gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the sparrow audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 4 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. A farm emitting 197 variations of one paragraph hence pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the umber panel. That is 25 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
